title: Executive financial performance
question: How did revenue and operating profit change, and which months drove the result?
kpis: Gross margin=GP/revenue; operating margin=OP/revenue; YoY=(current/prior−1); percentage changes use percentage points.
logic: LAG over annual results and same calendar month; cumulative SUM resets each year.
limitations: Initial-year YoY is NULL. OP follows approved policy; net income and cash flow are outside scope.

title: Product profitability
question: Which products create profit and how do realized prices compare with COGS per unit?
kpis: GP=revenue−five-component COGS; contribution=GP−outbound; realized price=revenue/shipped units.
logic: DENSE_RANK and cumulative contribution ordered by gross profit; annual ratio-of-sums with same-product LAG.
limitations: Product contribution excludes unallocated company opex and idle losses. Price/cost changes are descriptive, not causal price-volume-mix attribution.

title: Manufacturing costs and activity drivers
question: Which cost components dominate, and what drives line conversion economics?
kpis: Manufacturing total=five components; labor rate=cost/hours; energy tariff=cost/kWh; activity intensity=activity/attempted units.
logic: LATERAL VALUES unpivots only five authoritative components; line pools analyzed independently from allocations.
limitations: Never add cost pools to product allocations, or landed material subtotal to purchase/freight. Manufacturing additions differ from sales COGS because inventory defers costs.

title: Production efficiency and defects
question: Which lines have capacity pressure and where are defects concentrated?
logic: Ratios of annual sums, annual LAG changes and defect-count ranking; no sales joins.
limitations: Capacity utilization is not OEE. No machine-speed or quality inspection detail; defect volume depends on production mix. No scrap-sale recovery assumption.

title: Supplier performance and procurement
question: How concentrated is purchasing, and do observed receipts support supplier comparisons?
sources: suppliers LEFT JOIN bi_procurement_receipts; material receipt details
grain: Q1 supplier/full period; Q2 material/receipt year
kpis: OTD=on-time receipt count/all observed receipts; lead days=receipt−order; purchase price=purchase EUR/kg.
logic: Retains suppliers without receipts; COUNT(receipt_id) avoids counting null extended rows; weighted spend/quantity rates.
limitations: Suppliers with zero receipts have NULL performance, not zero OTD. Synthetic scheduled/full receipts limit real supplier reliability conclusions. Receipt-based OTD is not order-line fill rate.

title: Inventory valuation and turnover
question: How much cost is tied up in inventory and how quickly does it turn?
kpis: FG turns=annual COGS/mean monthly midpoint FG; raw turns=annual landed issues/mean raw midpoint; combined days=calendar days*mean combined inventory/COGS.
logic: Aggregate each inventory fact to month before joining; average (opening+closing)/2 across months; calendar carries actual 365/366 days.
limitations: Midpoints approximate time-average balances; zero opening FG in 2024 creates startup bias. No WIP, daily balances or receivables/payables: this is not a cash conversion cycle. Closing balances are not summed across months.

title: Customer concentration
question: How dependent is revenue on the largest customers, and does their contribution justify concentration?
kpis: Revenue share=customer/year revenue divided by company/year; HHI=sum of squared percentage shares; contribution=GP−outbound.
logic: Annual customer aggregation, deterministic ROW_NUMBER ties by customer_id, cumulative revenue windows and conditional top-N sums.
limitations: HHI describes this fictional customer book, not an antitrust market measure. No contract renewal, credit risk or group ownership data; customer contribution excludes shared opex.

title: Logistics and distribution
question: How do outbound distribution costs differ by segment and how is inbound freight recognized?
grain: Q1 year/customer segment; Q2 year freight recognition bridge
kpis: Outbound EUR/unit=freight/shipped; distribution burden=outbound/revenue; inbound receipt amounts are capitalized, not immediately expensed.
logic: Segment ratios of sums; independent annual receipt and sales aggregates joined to calendar-year spine.
limitations: Inbound purchases and recognized inbound COGS differ through inventory. Outbound is below GP, never inventory. Rates are synthetic blended per-unit costs; geography and minimum shipment charges are absent.
